verdict.rationale: Checkout.com documents HMAC-signed webhooks for payment lifecycle events. They can be managed via the Dashboard or API, can be resent (a replay mechanism), and can be delivered to Amazon EventBridge. The evidence does not cover automatic delivery retries or a browsable event or delivery log. The idempotency retry docs concern client API request retries, not webhook redelivery. Missing for 10: documented automatic webhook retry policy/schedule, event/delivery log visibility, details of the resend/replay flow, independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a developer, I can rely on signed webhook deliveries with automatic retries, event logs, and replay to keep my system consistent with payment state

citations.quote: Webhooks are automated messages that Checkout.com sends your server when events related to your account occur. For example, payment lifecycle activity, changes to balances, or progress on disputes.

Signatures use HMAC; webhook config is manageable "using the Dashboard or the API", with documented sub-pages for configuring the webhook server, managing webhooks via API, resending webhooks, and receiving events in Amazon EventBridge.
